tools_found.signal_summary: AMD's AI Group has used Claude Code intensively for complex systems/GPU engineering, running dozens of concurrent autonomous agent sessions. AMD Senior Director of AI Stella Laurenzo publicly documented this usage in detail (6,852 sessions, 234,760 tool calls) while filing a regression complaint, confirming substantial real internal use.

evidence.claim: AMD Senior Director of AI Group Stella Laurenzo filed a public GitHub issue describing her team's heavy internal use of Claude Code for high-complexity engineering (systems programming in C, MLIR, GPU drivers), including 50+ concurrent agent sessions and 30+ minute autonomous runs, and concluded after a February/March 2026 regression that 'Claude cannot be trusted to perform complex engineering.'
evidence.quote: Claude has regressed to the point it cannot be trusted to perform complex engineering.

evidence.claim: The Register reports Stella Laurenzo is director of the AI group at AMD and analyzed months of logs (6,852 Claude Code sessions, 234,760 tool calls, 17,871 thinking blocks) from 'a very consistent, high complexity work environment' used by her team.
evidence.quote: very consistent, high complexity work environment

evidence.claim: PC Gamer / TechRadar coverage identifies the author as AMD's senior director of AI and describes her team's prior productive use of Claude Code for kernel-level and hardware-adjacent engineering before the reported regression.

Laurenzo's analysis describes her team's prior workflow: during February, 1,498 API requests produced ~191,000 lines of merged code; by early March they scaled to 5-10+ concurrent Claude Code sessions across 10 projects including IREE (loom, amdgpu, remoting, batteries, web, fuzzing) and an internal multi-agent system named 'Bureau', with agents running autonomously 30+ minutes.

tools_found.signal_summary: AMD's AMD-AGI organization ships an open-source RL/agent pipeline (Apex) that uses OpenAI Codex as one of three selectable agent backends to autonomously optimize GPU kernels for AMD ROCm hardware. This is genuine internal engineering tooling built and used by AMD, not a product integration sold to customers.

evidence.claim: The AMD-AGI/Apex repository (maintained by Advanced Micro Devices) optimizes bottleneck GPU kernels for ROCm via 'Claude Code or Codex', supporting Codex as an --agent-backend option requiring an active OpenAI account.
evidence.quote: optimizes them via Claude Code or Codex, and scores on compilation, correctness, and speedup

tools_found.signal_summary: AMD's AMD-AGI Apex GPU-kernel-optimization pipeline lists Cursor Agent (with agent mode enabled) as a third selectable agent backend alongside Claude Code and Codex, indicating AMD-built tooling that can drive Cursor's agent for kernel optimization.

evidence.claim: AMD-AGI/Apex README documents three agent backends for kernel optimization: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and 'Cursor Agent (Cursor) — requires a Cursor subscription with agent mode enabled', selectable via the --agent-backend flag (claude default, codex, or cursor).
evidence.quote: Cursor Agent (Cursor) — requires a Cursor subscription with agent mode enabled
